passage:
At the Cape Town schools' swimming gala, Siddiq touched the wall a full second slower than the qualifying time he needed. He hung on the lane rope, chest heaving, watching the board.
Thabo, who had beaten him last term, leaned over from the next lane. "Was that your best? Maybe the regional team isn't for you." A couple of his friends laughed.
Siddiq felt his jaw clench. He wanted to fire back. Instead he pulled himself out, dried his face and said, "Well swum." Thabo blinked and walked off.
That evening Siddiq wrote his time on the kitchen whiteboard, next to his best from last month. "Beat this one," he wrote underneath. His father added a smiley.

qa.q: What did Thabo say to Siddiq at the gala?
qa.a: He said, "Was that your best? Maybe the regional team isn't for you."

qa.q: How did Siddiq feel when Thabo gloated, and what did he do with that feeling?
qa.a: He felt angry, his jaw clenching as he wanted to fire back, but he held back, said 'Well swum' and put his effort into beating his own time.

qa.q: What was wise about writing his time on the whiteboard?
qa.a: It turned his attention from the rival to his own past score, giving him something he could actually work on.

qa.q: What might Thabo have been feeling when he leaned over the lane rope?
qa.a: Thabo may have been keen to stay ahead, since he had beaten Siddiq before, and his surprise at 'Well swum' suggests he expected an argument.

grounding: A rival gloats over Siddiq's failure; he doesn't stoop, and aims to beat his own past score.
